Two theater retirements, one PR

plan · before/after · verified at HEAD 2026-08-01, including one correction to my own inventory
Correction first. The inventory called this "the weekly eval cron". Wrong — orchestkit-eval.yml is workflow_dispatch: only, with a comment forbidding re-adding schedules (the no-LLM-in-CI policy already de-scheduled it). What remains is worse in a quieter way: a manual tool that produces fake numbers on demand. A plan built on the stale claim would have "fixed" the wrong thing.

Fix A — retire the prose-grading eval pipeline

Before — what a dispatch actually runs

operator: gh workflow run orchestkit-eval
   |
   v
unit + security + typecheck
   all continue-on-error
   = CI proper, re-run worse
   |
   v
scripts/run-eval.sh
   |
   +- "Phase 1: Trigger Detection"
   |    grades description CLARITY,
   |    not trigger accuracy
   |
   +- "Phase 2: Structure Validation"
   |    duplicates test:skills
   |
   +- 5 RANDOM skills (sort -R)
   |    claude -p "Rate this AI skill
   |    description 1-10..."
   |
   v
"Eval Summary" — numbers that
read like skill quality, measure
description wording of a random 5

After — the fakes are gone, the real ones named

orchestkit-eval.yml   DELETED
scripts/run-eval.sh   DELETED
   |
   v
every phase had a real successor
already running:

behavioral quality
  skill-eval.yml — per changed
  skill, baseline vs with-skill,
  budgeted, watched live 07-20

routing accuracy
  eval-routing.yml — PR gate
  on the 50-pair benchmark

trigger keywords
  test-trigger-keywords.sh —
  deterministic, in ci.yml

unit/security/typecheck
  ci.yml proper — blocking,
  not continue-on-error
Why delete rather than fix. Every phase is either fake (prose grading, the misnamed trigger eval) or a worse duplicate of a blocking CI job. "Adoption is subtraction" is this repo's own written policy — the successors are already live, so the honest fix is removal plus a registry-changelog tombstone, not renovation.

Fix B — give task-nudge-outcomes.jsonl a reader

Before — signal without a consumer

Stop hook writes (#3232, ≤2/session)
  .claude/logs/task-nudge-outcomes.jsonl
  { qualifying_prompts, tasks_used }
   |
   v
readers ............ 0
telemetry-inspect
  inventory row .... absent
  (the skill that EXISTS to catch
   orphan telemetry would flag
   its own repo's newest file)
   |
   v
day-old proto-theater:
a number nobody can see

After — the number is one command away

scripts/analytics/task-compliance.mjs
  reads the jsonl, prints:

  sessions w/ qualifying work: 12
  of which used tasks:          9
  compliance:                 75%
  trend vs prior week:        +25pt

telemetry-inspect
  references/telemetry-inventory.md
  row added: writer + READER named

hooks README changelog
  nudge entry updated: telemetry
  now names its consumer
The standard this enforces. The cure for theater everywhere in this session was pairing a claim with something that reads it. Same rule applied to my own six-hour-old telemetry before it calcifies: writer + reader + inventory row, or it does not ship.
